page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It is equipped with 2835 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong performance in compute-intensive and memory-access tasks. It achieves a PassMark CPU score of 66237.87 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 302.08 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 36.36 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier. For database operations, the server processes 79.57 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 22353.15 on PassMark database tests. Small-model LLM inference yields 338.79 tokens/sec for text generation. However, the primary tradeoff is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-bound workloads despite its high computational throughput.

The qualitative cost profile of the D48lds_v7 reflects a compute-heavy design with reduced memory overhead. By minimizing memory capacity relative to the 48 vCPUs, the server offers a resource-dense option for workloads that require high CPU clock speeds and local storage but do not demand large RAM footprints. This makes the server appropriate for compute-optimized tasks, web serving, file compression, and database operations that fit within the 96.0 GB memory limit.
